title: Capability
description: One slice of a product's partition — a claim about part of what the product can do. Capabilities of a product are intended to be exhaustive and non-overlapping; the database cannot verify that (see coverage_review), so scope_boundary is mandatory as the cheap defence. Source: supabase/migrations/002_product_and_capability.sql

product_id.description: FK -> product.id. IMMUTABLE after insert: a BEFORE UPDATE trigger rejects any change. To move a capability, create it under the new product and deprecate this one.

key.description: Slug, unique per (product_id, key). Stored as citext, so uniqueness is CASE-INSENSITIVE. The kebab-case pattern is project convention (e.g. 'telemetry-capture'), not a database CHECK.

description.description: What this capability is, in the customer's terms. Distinct from scope_boundary, which says where it ends. Carries the text formerly held by value_prop, renamed in 020 because value proposition is a Feature property only — see feature.schema.json#/properties/value_prop, which is jsonb and means something else entirely. Source: supabase/migrations/020_capability_description.sql

scope_boundary.description: What is IN and explicitly what is OUT. The only defence against overlapping capabilities, which would break the partition. Convention is an 'In: ... Out: ...' pair naming the neighbouring capabilities.

status.description: capability_status enum. 'proposed' scores 0 and is excluded from the product's vbo partition, so adding a capability never forces the rest to be rescored. 'archived' scores 0 because it offers nothing. Only 'active' and 'deprecated' may carry a positive vbo; deprecated keeps one so it can be tuned toward zero across a sunset. Source: supabase/migrations/017_capability_scoring.sql

visibility.description: visibility enum. Gates exposure through v_capability_catalog.

updated_at.description: Maintained by the private.touch_updated_at() BEFORE UPDATE trigger; a client-supplied value is overwritten.

vbo.description: Vital Business Offering: this capability's authored share of the product, in percentage points. AUTHORED, never derived — compare against the capability_weight view to find drift between what a capability is supposed to carry and what it measurably does. The vbo of a product's ACTIVE capabilities sums to 100; that rule spans rows, so it is reported by v_model_health as 'vbo_does_not_sum' rather than enforced by a constraint. The per-row half IS enforced: a capability that is not active or deprecated must be 0.

$comment: KPIs are not properties here: a capability's measured metrics live in capability_kpi (capability_id, name), a junction rather than an array so 'which capabilities track this metric' is an indexed lookup.
